note: Signed comparison difference, not missing emissions or a bound. NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE, but the mismatch is now one category rather than four. EDGAR Processes covers cement, lime, soda ash, ammonia, and iron and steel. Since rc52 the engine estimates three of those five - cement 21.8156 (trade-corrected calcination), ammonia 3.2433, iron and steel 0.3931 - and adds lubricant use 0.0833, which EDGAR's row does not name: an IPPU module of 25.5354 Mt, 0.93 of EDGAR's 27.38. Lime (2.A.2) is NE for want of activity data. Soda ash (2.B.7) is NA rather than NE: the Solvay-process carbon is allocated to Energy under IPCC Vol.3 s3.8.3.1, so it cannot be counted as a missing IPPU term. The residual 1.84 Mt is therefore of the order of one absent category. Cement alone is 0.80 of the whole-processes row; its own valid FY2023-24 Tier-1 configurations give 17.39 Mt at a 0.75 clinker fraction and 21.50 Mt at 0.95, so cement spans 64-80% of the EDGAR row depending on configuration. The engine column of THIS ROW is the cement term alone (engine_category resolves to the 2.A.1 category), which is why it reads 21.82 and not the 25.5354 module total; the module ratio is stated in the manuscript beside it. Excludes the 11.54 Mt of F-gases EDGAR reports separately, which this inventory does not estimate at all.
